✅ review — accepted

Recorded by agent (unattended review-loop) via the declared `review-pr` operation (#3035).

## Human review verdict — web-everything/web-everything#7289

**Verdict:** ✅ pass — no blocking findings
**Disposition:** converge — an agent may land it on an accept verdict

### Panel verdicts

| lens | weight | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| correctness (codex) | mandatory | accept |

### Findings (7)

**correctness/COVERAGE** (7)
- `backlog/xnulgp5-map-we-maturity-levels-to-everstandards-maturity.md:22` — COVERAGE: The maturity-mapping acceptance criteria have no named planned tests. — A1–A3 request a documentation review and unspecified affected vectors, but identify no test file, case or assertion. A plausible later implementation could export Draft or Stable by default when evidence is absent. Proposed checks: we:__tests__/maturity-export.test.mjs cases `missing_evidence_exports_no_stage`, `experimental_without_vectors_is_not_candidate`, `active_without_implementation_is_not_stable`, and `stable_requires_two_independent_pinned_passes`; a named documentation check should cover correspondence differences and unchanged source statuses. These are proposed tests, not supplied ones. Mutation verification was impossible with the read-only shell. _[CONFIRMED]_ _[impact if unfixed: degraded]_
  - _Prevention (OWED — file it):_ Add a deterministic card gate requiring each Acceptance ID to reference a named planned check, repository-qualified file and observable assertion.
- `backlog/xcfikoo-reconcile-we-conformance-level-scales-and-stale-maturity-ref.md:24` — COVERAGE: None of the level-reconciliation acceptance criteria identifies a named check. — A1–A3 require separate axes, evidence for every mapping row and an accurate implementation-rule citation, but supply no named tests or review cases. A plausible documentation update could still silently equate manifest L1 with assertion L1 or describe the blocks-only warning as universal. Proposed checks in we:__tests__/conformance-level-mapping.test.mjs: `axes_remain_distinct`, `every_mapping_row_has_proof`, and `implementation_reference_matches_rule_scope`. Mutation verification was impossible with the read-only shell; these checks are proposed only. _[CONFIRMED]_ _[impact if unfixed: degraded]_
  - _Prevention (OWED — file it):_ Require structured Acceptance-to-check references, including named documentation checks for documentation-only work.
- `backlog/xsw08od-run-hybrid-step-5-kernel-ci-heal-in-shadow-against-ship-draf.md:23` — COVERAGE: The shadow-run card leaves its acceptance safeguards without named planned tests. — A1–A3 name categories of verification but no test cases. A plausible harness could report zero differences after dropping unmatched decisions or during a disabled tap, or permit effects despite being called shadow. Proposed cases in longshore:packages/kernel/test/ci-heal-shadow.test.mjs: `requires_pinned_ship_drafts`, `missing_decision_counts_as_diff`, `tap_gap_invalidates_soak`, `requires_24_hours_and_predeclared_differences`, `replay_preserves_actions`, `crash_and_unknown_input_refuse_effects`, and `shadow_cannot_write_forge`. The last must observe denied or absent writes, not merely configuration. Mutation verification was impossible with the read-only shell. _[CONFIRMED]_ _[impact if unfixed: degraded]_
  - _Prevention (OWED — file it):_ Gate prepared implementation cards on a structured mapping from every acceptance safeguard to a named planned negative test and assertion.
- `backlog/8629-when-do-github-labels-stop-being-the-source-of-truth.md` — COVERAGE: Migration and authority guarantees lack named planned regression checks. — The new command-ingestion and switch rules identify no named tests. The same gap affects #5488's switch/rollback guarantees, #5785's journal safety and single-authority rules, and #8634's migration invariants. Plausible later implementations could discard genuine commands as echoes, revive approvals during rollback, or lose cards from queues. Proposed checks include longshore:packages/forge/test/commands.test.mjs::shared_identity_does_not_imply_echo and ::clear_requires_reviewed_head; longshore:packages/kernel/test/authority.test.mjs::unreadable_register_refuses and ::rollback_imports_holds_not_approvals; longshore:packages/store/test/journal.test.mjs::crash_recovery_never_reuses_seq and ::multiple_hosts_refuse_journal_authority; longshore:packages/backlog/test/migration.test.mjs::preserves_aliases_and_queue_membership. No such named mapping is supplied. Mutation verification was impossible with the read-only shell. _[CONFIRMED]_ _[impact if unfixed: degraded]_
  - _Prevention (OWED — file it):_ Require every prepared must-hold rule to carry an identifier and a named planned check; reject unresolved references deterministically.
- `backlog/8623-use-one-template-for-every-everstandard.md` — COVERAGE: The proposed conformance and release gates are not mapped to named tests. — The card promises unmapped requirements fail CI, disputes/exclusions block Stable, features cannot weaken MUSTs and independence is enforced, but names no defending tests. Related guarantees in #8630, #8632, #8626 and #8627 likewise lack named checks for Candidate evidence, unknown verdict conversion, identifier publication and moved-runner equivalence. A plausible implementation could accept a default maturity value or convert unknown into success. Proposed cases in everstandards/conformance:test/release-gates.test.mjs include `unmapped_requirement_fails`, `disputed_or_excluded_requirement_blocks_stable`, `feature_cannot_weaken_must`, `stable_requires_independent_pinned_passes`, `candidate_requires_live_pass`, `unknown_never_maps_to_vsa_passed`, and `publication_requires_absolute_owned_namespace`; moved-runner fixtures need named equivalence cases. These are proposed only; mutation verification was impossible with the read-only shell. _[CONFIRMED]_ _[impact if unfixed: degraded]_
  - _Prevention (OWED — file it):_ Extend the preparation gate to require named positive and negative checks for each conformance or release guarantee, explicitly covering omitted/default values.
- `backlog/8625-should-we-use-workflow-profiles-with-no-expressions-and-dura.md` — COVERAGE: Workflow failure and default semantics have no named planned tests. — The card specifies mandatory unknown routing, missing-classifier behavior, pure classifiers, compensation order and a default of continue after compensation failure, but supplies no named tests; #8633 also promises soundness and disclosed conversion losses without named cases. A plausible implementation could test explicit continue while an omitted setting halts, or silently discard unsupported adapter behavior. Proposed cases in everstandards/flow:conformance/workflow.test.mjs: `missing_classifier_routes_unknown`, `unknown_cannot_authorize_effect`, `classifier_cannot_change_state`, `compensation_respects_reverse_dependencies`, `omitted_failure_policy_continues_with_visible_failure`, and `unsupported_conversion_reports_loss`. Mutation verification was impossible with the read-only shell. _[CONFIRMED]_ _[impact if unfixed: degraded]_
  - _Prevention (OWED — file it):_ Require named planned tests for explicit, omitted and invalid values whenever a prepared card introduces a behavioral default.
- `backlog/8635-unpause-the-builder-for-stage-1-after-all-four-preconditions.md` — COVERAGE: Builder readiness and operator-setting boundaries lack named planned checks. — The mechanical conditional-go proposal names no tests proving each missing prerequisite keeps the builder paused, installed evidence is required, scope/caps hold or rollback restores the pause. Related #8628 and #5411 guarantees that operator values never become product defaults also lack named checks. A plausible implementation could activate from incomplete evidence or ship the operator's two-lane value as a generic default. Proposed cases in we:__tests__/builder-readiness.test.mjs: `each_missing_proof_keeps_paused`, `merge_without_installation_is_insufficient`, `g2_g3_require_explicit_disposition`, and `rollback_restores_zero_caps`; longshore:packages/settings/test/defaults.test.mjs::other_repos_defaults_to_zero and ::team_values_are_not_product_defaults. These are proposed tests; mutation verification was impossible with the read-only shell. _[CONFIRMED]_ _[impact if unfixed: degraded]_
  - _Prevention (OWED — file it):_ Require named planned checks for every activation prerequisite and operator/product default boundary before a preparation card is considered test-mapped.

---

**Decision:** `accept` — recorded by agent (unattended review-loop).
**Lenses:** `correctness` — 1 juror(s), one per lens, each a separate `judge` step spawned with its own derived session id (#3028) and its own tools (#3319). They ran SEQUENTIALLY and neither saw the other's findings; this is not a `judgePanel` fan-out (#3050). The other 4 panel lens(es) (security, simplicity, standards-conformance, claim-accuracy) did NOT run and are not reported as unjudged.
**Earned vs seated:** this PR's prose touch-set scores care `none`, for which the care dial asks for 0 lens(es) × 0 juror(s)/lens × 0 round(s). This run seated 1 lens(es) (correctness), 1 juror each, in 1 round. No lens shortfall: every lens the touch-set earned sat. The caller declared no `--careLevel`, so nothing checked the shape this run was dialled for against the files it actually judged (#3335). The shortfall is structural — the step list is fixed at registration (#3319) — so it is RECORDED here rather than implied away: do not read the seats above as the whole review this PR earned.
Net basis: `949455066f8810cc471d8847f737b5d59865cfd8..e9d5d574f98e62d0bd46f42c6a881de8a048f2f8` (rev `origin/lane/decision-items-prepared` at review time) — 21 net changed file(s) vs current main (#2450), not `gh pr diff`'s three-dot list.
